notes:
The question 'Do they hold 24x7 Enterprise support?' changes nothing in the database; the seed answers it no (no entitlement for product 139; the account-wide enterprise 24x7 entitlement 75 is inactive and its contract 138 expired), so the conditional procurement applies.
The location name 'Stark Industries - New Lab' is an exact string the request does not fix; it is kept because the benchmark tests it, but an agent naming the site from the request's words (for example 'Stark Industries London Lab') fails that cell.
The contract's contract_type and price are not tested: the request calls it a contract extension for 24x7 Enterprise support but does not fix the type, and the expired contract it replaces is a warranty contract.
The case short_description follows a policy template the benchmark does not test, so it is not a cell.
No listed tool creates interactions, though the policy requires one per new case.
Group assignment (group 2) and user assignment (user 127) are separate requirements: the request names only the group, and the user is the benchmark's choice among the active members of group 2.
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass tests the case's group, assignee and state in one requirement, the other gives the assignee (user 127) a requirement of its own; kept the separate assignee requirement because the request names only the group and the assignee is the benchmark's choice, so the group assignment is scored on its own; the cells tested are the same either way.

disagreement: value: the interaction's contact_id: one pass leaves it untested, the other tests contact 10; kept it because the interaction records the case's reporting contact, which the case requirement fixes as 10.
